name: NTT Berlin 1 Data Center
notes: Official NTT location page lists the Berlin 1 facility in Spandau with 11,700+ sq m of server space and 17.1 MW maximum IT load.

name: NTT Berlin 2 Data Center / Marienpark
notes: Official NTT pages place Berlin 2 at Lankwitzer Strasse 45-47 and state 24 MW maximum/initial IT capacity across buildings A and B.

name: VIRTUS Marienpark Campus (BERLIN1/BERLIN2)
notes: VIRTUS Germany locations page says the Marienpark campus comprises BERLIN1 and BERLIN2, four buildings totaling 62.6 MW IT load, set to go live in 2027; DCD reported the Berlin campus groundbreaking and 57.6 MW full build-out in May 2025.

name: Data Castle BER1 / in.grid Spandau
developer: DATA CASTLE GmbH / Data Center Group
notes: Data Center Group project page describes BER1 in Berlin Spandau with 40 MVA total capacity, 26 MW IT load, 10,000 sq m IT area, completion planned end-2025; DCD reported Data Castle as new owner in 2023.

name: NorthC Berlin redevelopment data center (Berlin 2)
notes: NorthC announced entry into Berlin through redevelopment of an existing building, 3 MW initial IT load with growth potential to 8 MW; Berlin 2 page now markets carrier- and cloud-neutral colocation.

name: maincubes BER01 GoWest Berlin
notes: Official maincubes page lists BER01 in Berlin on the GoWest campus as in operation, 9 MW IT capacity and 55,000 sq ft whitespace.

name: nLighten Berlin edge data center
notes: Official nLighten location page lists its Berlin edge data center with 3,894 sq m dedicated colocation space and 1,800 kW of power.

name: Penta Infra BER01
notes: Official Penta Infra page lists BER01 at Florastrasse 133-135, 12623 Berlin-Marzahn-Hellersdorf with 2.7 MW IT capacity and growth opportunities (former DB Systel DC); BCIX peering member.

name: Microsoft Azure Germany North (Berlin) cloud region (seed)
notes: Cloud-region seed: Azure Germany North is paired with Germany West Central (Frankfurt) per official Microsoft geography docs; region-level evidence only - no physical facility inference.

name: Google Cloud Berlin-Brandenburg region (seed)
notes: Cloud-region seed: Google Cloud Berlin-Brandenburg region opened 2023; official region-level evidence spanning Berlin/Brandenburg - no physical facility inference.

name: Rechenzentrum Seefeld, Werneuchen
notes: City of Werneuchen public notice: Satzungsbeschluss made the Bebauungsplan 'Rechenzentrum Seefeld' effective; MOZ reports the bylaw decision and uncertainty about start timing.

name: Rechenzentrum Eiche, Ahrensfelde
notes: Ahrensfelde municipal planning portal identifies Bebauungsplan 'Rechenzentrum Eiche' east of Eiche at Mehrower Weg on former greenhouse land; local reporting describes investor plan for a high-tech data center.

name: Britz / Eberswalde Gewerbegebiet data center plan
notes: MOZ reported an investor wants to build four data centers in the Britz industrial area near Eberswalde; later reporting noted interest from Italian and US companies.

name: Projektierter Neubau eines Rechenzentrums (real-estate listing)
notes: ImmoScout24 listing 'Projektierter Neubau eines hochmodernen Rechenzentrums' in 14776 Brandenburg an der Havel (Dom area). Marketing-grade lead only; no official planning/permit documentation found in targeted searches.

name: Med Areal Cottbus geothermal data center concept
notes: Official Med Areal page markets a Cottbus data center solution using geothermal energy, photovoltaics and passive-house technology; no MW capacity or construction milestone found.

name: Vantage Berlin II Data Center Campus, Mittenwalde
notes: Official Vantage page gives campus address at Dahmestrasse 1 and 2, 15749 Mittenwalde; DataCenterMap describes two buildings at the Berlin II campus with 16 MW each (32 MW campus); supported by 380-kV grid connection proceeding BK4-20-028 via Umspannwerk Thyrow (see grid record).

name: Google Berlin-Brandenburg / Mittenwalde data center site
notes: Google abandoned plans for a data center near Schenkendorf/Mittenwalde in Dahme-Spreewald after previously buying a 30-hectare site.

name: 380-kV-Netzanschluss Rechenzentrum Mittenwalde (Umspannwerk Thyrow)
notes: Bundesnetzagentur proceeding BK4-20-028 / 50Hertz: 380-kV grid connection for a data center in Mittenwalde area via Umspannwerk Thyrow; NEP 2037/2045 draft lists 'Thyrow: 380-kV-Netzanschluss (Rechenzentrum Genshagen)'. Grid evidence supports the Vantage Berlin II campus and general large-load allocation in the area.

name: AWS European Sovereign Cloud data center, Massen-Niederlausitz / Finsterwalde
developer: Amazon Web Services (AWS European Sovereign Cloud GmbH)
notes: Elbe-Elster county welcomed AWS locating a central part of the European Sovereign Cloud in Massen; DataCenter-Insider reported earthworks and container village at the Massen industrial park near Finsterwalde; regional reporting gives ~200 MW; Amazon announced EUR 7.8bn for the first sovereign region in Brandenburg (Massen + Baruth/Mark).

name: Frankfurt DATA FFO AI hyperscale campus, Markendorf
developer: Frankfurt Data AI GmbH (projektentwickler, Technologiepark Frankfurt (Oder))
notes: Stadtverordnetenversammlung of Frankfurt (Oder) unanimously created the planning prerequisites (2026-03-30) for a hyperscale data center in the Markendorf industrial park at B87; up to EUR 3.5bn investment and up to 350 MW connection capacity (330-360 MW reported); waste heat to feed municipal district heating; project depends on a 380-kV grid connection.

name: VIRTUS Wustermark Campus
notes: Official VIRTUS page describes the Wustermark campus as up to nine data centers delivering 204 MW IT load (300 MW incoming power); DCD reported construction began April 2026 with EUR 3bn investment; two 185MVA super-grid transformers installed June 2026; 50Hertz signed a 300-MW grid contract and extends Umspannwerk Wustermark for a 380-kV connection.

name: maincubes BER02 / mainHub Berlin Campus, Nauen
notes: Official maincubes pages place BER02/mainHub in Nauen with up to 144-186 MW IT capacity and a 200 MW grid connection agreement; zoning approved, land purchase 2024; rbb24 reports Spatenstich March 2026 (substation first plus 6 km line to Wustermark, six ~28 m-high data centers on a 15 ha campus at B5); first data center expected end-2027.

name: NTT Berlin 3 Data Center Campus, Brieselang
developer: NTT Global Data Centers / NTT DATA
notes: NTT announced a third Berlin campus in Brieselang, 30 km west of Berlin, on a 10.8 ha site with 96 MW critical IT load across two data centers; construction expected to start in 2025.

name: ZAE Projekt GmbH Rechenzentrum, Fredersdorf-Vogelsdorf
notes: rbb24 and MOZ reported ZAE Projekt GmbH plans a data center on an 11.8 ha site at the edge of Fredersdorf-Vogelsdorf between A10 and B1, facing local opposition; MW capacity not found.

name: Colt DCS Berlin 1 and Berlin 2
notes: Colt official page and trade press say it secured land 10 km east of Berlin for Berlin 1 and 2, two Tier 3 hyperscale data centers delivering 54 MW IT load (part of 117 MW Germany expansion with Frankfurt 4/5). Assigned to Märkisch-Oderland based on east-of-Berlin Brandenburg location (Neuenhagen/Hoppegarten area); exact municipality not disclosed.

name: Schwarz Digits Datacenter Lübbenau
notes: Official Schwarz Digits page: EUR 11bn data center being built in Lübbenau on the former power-plant site (13 ha), Spatenstich 2025-11-17, up to 200 MW connection capacity, up to 100,000 GPUs, first phase by end-2027; green power plus waste-heat feed into district heating.

name: Freyenstein AI data center campus, Wittstock/Dosse
developer: Anonymous German investor (Serban DC / Noya Generalplanung und Projektmanagement GmbH per market listings)
notes: DCD reports a 700 MW data center proposal outside Freyenstein (Wittstock/Dosse, Ostprignitz-Ruppin) on ~144-150 ha, estimated EUR 25bn, with no local planning permission yet and grid-connection questions pending at 50Hertz; opposition petition cites 700 MW IT / ~1,008 MW total; project presented to residents April 2026.

name: Michendorf former Telekom site data center proposal
notes: MAZ reports the plan to build a data center on the former Telekom site in Michendorf was withdrawn / off the table after local debate; earlier MAZ coverage described a Berlin investor seeking to develop the site.

name: Vantage BER1 / Berlin I campus, Ludwigsfelde
notes: Market listings identify Vantage BER1 / Berlin I at Uferring 5, 14974 Ludwigsfelde in Brandenburg Park, four buildings at full buildout and 56 MW critical IT load (474,000 sq ft); Vantage lists the Berlin I Germany campus at the same Ludwigsfelde address; NEP draft lists 380-kV Netzanschluss 'Rechenzentrum Genshagen' via Umspannwerk Thyrow as supporting grid evidence.

name: AWS European Sovereign Cloud campus, Baruth/Mark
developer: Amazon Web Services (AWS European Sovereign Cloud GmbH)
notes: Regional reporting (niederlausitz-aktuell, flaemont.de, ayedo) places part of the AWS European Sovereign Cloud first Brandenburg region in Baruth/Mark (~100 MW), alongside Massen/Finsterwalde (200 MW); initially over leased data centers, with own infrastructure being built; Baruth/Mark is in Teltow-Fläming.

name: Trebbin data center proposal
developer: Unnamed developer / SDC Capital Partners referenced in market listings
notes: DCD reports the Trebbin council could not approve the scheme due to questions including building height; MAZ described an investor planning a data center on a commercial plot in Trebbin; Baxtel market context references SDC Capital Partners planning a data center on a 23-acre Trebbin site.

name: NEOIX Wünsdorf AI data center
notes: NEOIX says its 30 MW data center development in Wünsdorf, Brandenburg received preliminary approval and will test advanced cooling and renewable integration. Wünsdorf is in Zossen, Teltow-Fläming.

name: Landkreis Uckermark modular data center procurement, Prenzlau
notes: Public-tender aggregator summarizing procurement documents says Landkreis Uckermark is buying a prefabricated modular data center, 40 kW / 6 racks, to be delivered and commissioned at Prenzlau by 2027.

name: b.r.m. IT & Aerospace green data center, Bremen Airport
notes: Operator site describes its Bremen location and long-standing green IT / sustainable data center work; company address Hanna-Kunath-Strasse 31, Bremen.

name: SIEVERS Bremen data center (former nuclear shelter)
notes: DCD reports SIEVERS opened a Tier 4-certified 2,000 sqm facility in a former nuclear shelter in Bremen, operational June 26, 2025; DataCenterMap lists SIEVERS Bremen at Zwinglistrasse 31.

name: LWLcom Bremen data centers (BRE01)
notes: Official LWLcom page describes its central Bremen data centers connected to its own fiber network (colocation, dedicated servers); directory listings put BRE01 at Pastorenweg 70 with ~900 sqm whitespace. Capacity not disclosed.

name: ColocationIX DC1 (ex-atomic bunker)
notes: ColocationIX operates a high-security colocation data center in a converted former federal atomic-shelter bunker in Bremen (Wachtstrasse 17-24); DataCenter-Insider/WFB Bremen coverage; multiple ColocationIX Bremen facilities per directory listings.
